AfterCombatVictory.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and N2 per binding rule 4. The room-type gate is right (RoomType.Elite only, executed) but the QUANTITY is not: C# upgrades exactly CardsVar(4) randomly chosen upgradable deck cards and the port upgrades EVERY upgradable card in the deck (G1), and the Rng.Niche stream the choice consumes is never touched (N2).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the port upgrades EVERY upgradable card in the deck where C# upgrades exactly 4
guards.issue: MECHANISM: WarHammer.cs:26-27 is `Deck.Cards.Where(c => c.IsUpgradable).ToList().StableShuffle(Rng.Niche).Take(Cards.IntValue)` with CanonicalVars = CardsVar(4) (WarHammer.cs:17) -- a random FOUR. war_hammer.py:20-22 is `for card in run.deck: if card.is_upgradable: card.upgrade()`, with no shuffle and no Take. The port's own docstring states the wrong behaviour as if it were the source's ('upgrade ALL upgradable cards in the deck', war_hammer.py:8-9), which is PROMPT.md bug class 19 in its most direct form: a wrong quantity protected by a confident citation of the C# file name. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py tools/audit/relic_probes_b17.py warhammer): one Elite victory with the starting deck upgrades all TEN cards (5 Strike, 4 Defend, Bash) where C# upgrades 4; a MONSTER victory upgrades 0 on both sides. Both sides ported: the relic is granted by the ported Tanx shrine and elites are a ported room type whose victory reaches RunState.finish_combat with room_type=ELITE. The divergence compounds -- the relic fires on EVERY elite victory, so a run with three elites upgrades the whole deck instead of at most 12 picks with replacement across a shrinking upgradable set, and sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:618 compares the deck as (id, upgrade_level) pairs, so any parity run that takes War Hammer diverges immediately. No ascension branch anywhere in WarHammer.cs, so 4 is the pinned non-ascension value. Rule 7: sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py and run.py are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: N3: C#'s hook is AfterCombatVictory; the sim's run-level after_combat_end is dispatched only on a non-fatal combat (run.py:1206-1208), and the port re-checks run.is_dead
guards.rationale: A naming trap worth pinning, because RelicModel.AfterCombatEnd and RelicModel.AfterCombatVictory are DIFFERENT C# hooks (relic/vambrace in this same batch uses the first, which fires on defeat too) and the sim exposes only one run-level method for both. RunState.finish_combat guards its dispatch with `if room_type is not None and not self.is_dead`, so the sim's run-level after_combat_end is in practice an AfterCombatVictory analogue -- the only way a combat ends without victory is the player dying, which sets run.is_dead. war_hammer.py:18 then re-checks `run.is_dead` redundantly. Equivalent observable, so faithful; flagged because a future relic implementing the real AfterCombatEnd through this same method would silently lose its defeat leg. Rule 7: run.py is NOT hashed here.

guards.what: N4: the ordering of the upgrades against the reward screen
guards.rationale: Checked because PROMPT.md bug class 25 makes multi-pass victory dispatch an ordering question, and audits/seam/hook_dispatch.json's class-25 note records AfterCombatVictoryEarly as a separate earlier full pass with relic/meat_on_the_bone as its only implementer. War Hammer implements the plain AfterCombatVictory pass, and its effect (deck upgrades) is read by nothing in the victory sequence: the sim runs finish_combat before generate_combat_rewards (run.py:1206-1208 then :1210-1213), and rewards.create_reward_cards builds options from the card POOL, not the deck. So no ordering against another victory listener changes its outcome. Rule 7: run.py, rewards.py and audits/seam/hook_dispatch.json are NOT hashed here.
